summary: Voters turn down a library's levy by a few votes, the library cuts staff and closes a floor, and a smaller levy passes a year later.
realLife: Gloversville voters rejected the library's budget in 2024 by 11 votes; the library laid off three workers, cut weekend hours and closed its upper floor. On May 20, 2025, voters approved a roughly $1 million budget with a 28.9 percent levy rise by 168 votes, and the library planned to reopen the floor and hire two workers. In Spokane, voters renewed a library levy in February 2024 that supplies about 18 percent of the library's budget, with officials saying hours and programs could be cut if it failed.
